Adani Group Skills and Education wing CEO Robin Bhowmik on Wednesday called for a major overhaul of India’s education system to bridge the growing gap between academic learning and industry requirements.

Speaking to MBA students at P.B. Siddhartha College of Arts and Science, he said that the country’s education system lacks adequate curricula to equip young people with industry-relevant skills. He stressed that education should not dictate career choices and urged students to focus on developing their personal capabilities to remain competitive in a rapidly changing job market.

Mr. Bhowmik highlighted Adani Group’s initiatives in skill development, including green energy training through its Centre of Excellence in Tirupati and plans to establish a skill academy in Visakhapatnam.

He also spoke about the group’s renewable energy project in Khavda, Gujarat, which has developed into the world’s largest hybrid renewable energy hub. Emphasising the group’s commitment to India’s development, he said it was investing substantially in education and public healthcare to support the vision of Viksit Bharat.

He identified the shortage of skilled human resources as a major challenge for the Adani Group and underscored the importance of anticipating future industry requirements.

College principal Meka Ramesh, director Vemuri Baburao, dean Rajesh C. Jampala, faculty members and students attended the programme.

articles.title: IAS officer Sajjan Singh Yadav assumes charge as Chief Secretary of J&K
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He joins at a time when the Chief Secretary post acts as the main interface between the Lok Bhavan and the Chief Minister’s office in the Union Territory (UT)
Dr. Sajjan Singh Yadav, a senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of 1995 batch, on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) formally took charge as the Chief Secretary of J&K.

Officials said senior administrative secretaries welcomed Mr. Yadav at the Civil Secretariat, Jammu. He made his first appearance at a police function held at the Sher-I-Kashmir Police Academy, Udhampur.

On October 24, 2026, Mr. Yadav was assigned the job. He joins at a time when the Chief Secretary post acts as the main interface between the Lok Bhavan and the Chief Minister’s office in the Union Territory (UT). Picked from the Arunachal Pradesh-Goa-Mizoram and Union Territories (AGMUT) cadre, Mr. Yadav’s will have to handle the most sticky files, including the Cabinet-approved files on regularisation of daily wagers, rationalisation of reservation and finalisation of Transaction of Business Rules, which remains undecided even after two years of completion of the Omar Abdullah government on October 16.

Mr. Yadav, a resident of Haryana, has a doctorate in Public Health from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine and Master’s in Public Policy, University of Minnesota. He brings in multi-sectoral experience as he served as Mission Director, National Nutrition Mission (POSHAN Abhiyan); Director, National Rural Health Mission; Commissioner of Food & Civil Supplies, Trade and Taxes, Excise in Delhi. This year, Mr. Yadav also served as Delhi Additional Chief Secretary and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Delhi Jal Board.

articles.title: India’s Oct. crude import bill soars 87.5% to $19.5-bn amid West Asia tensions, volumes up 11%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: While higher petroleum product exports offer a partial natural hedge, sustained increases in crude and gas prices could intensify pressure on the country’s import bill.

India’s crude oil import bill surged 87.5% year-on-year (YoY) to $19.5 billion in October, as elevated international benchmark prices, fuelled by renewed tensions in West Asia, sharply increased procurement costs. The increase came alongside an 11% rise in import volumes.

The net import bill, calculated as imports of crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas less exports of petroleum products, rose 60% to $16 billion during the month, compared with $10 billion in October last year.
Higher export realisations from petroleum products, however, provided some cushion against the escalating import burden.

According to provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), India imported 23.3 million metric tonnes (MMT) of crude oil in October, against 21 MMT in the corresponding month last year.
The expenditure on crude imports, meanwhile, climbed to $19.5 billion from $10.4 billion, reflecting the disproportionate impact of higher international prices on the country’s energy import bill.

The Indian crude oil basket averaged $119.91 per barrel in October, compared with $124.77 per barrel for Brent crude. In September, the Indian basket had averaged $116.09 per barrel, while Brent stood at $116.77 per barrel.

The sustained increase in benchmark prices, amid continuing geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia, has left India exposed to higher energy procurement costs, given its dependence on imported crude oil.
The impact of the rising crude import bill was partly offset by stronger earnings from petroleum product exports.
India’s petroleum product exports increased 5.9% in volume terms to 5.4 MMT in October. However, export revenues surged approximately 91% to $6.3 billion.
The increase in export earnings provided an important buffer against the higher cost of crude procurement.

articles.title: India-U.S. trade deal signing will still ‘take some time’, says Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: He added that the deal can be signed only after the U.S. finalises its new tariff framework. Recently, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the two nations had agreed that India would receive an advantage over its competitors

The actual signing of the India-U.S. trade will still “take some time”, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), adding that the negotiation part and the legal text will be completed soon.

The delay in signing, he said, was because it can be done only after the U.S. concludes its Section 301 investigations into its trade partners and finalises its tariff structure. A few days ago, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal asserted that the U.S. has acknowledged that India will receive lower tariffs as compared to its competitors.

“This is a deal that has been announced in February, the contours have already been announced as part of the joint statement,” Mr. Agrawal said while speaking at the curtain raiser of the FICCI Annual General Meeting. “The legal agreement has also been negotiated and it is now in final stages and it will be concluded soon.”
He was referring to the joint statement between India and the U.S. in February that announced the framework of an interim deal on trade.

However, Mr. Agrawal explained that the “challenge” is that this framework was announced against the background of the executive tariffs system that the U.S. President Donald Trump had put in place. At the time, the tariff on India was 50%. Later in February, the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the legal foundation of these tariffs.

“Now a new tariff architecture is being created by the U.S.,” Mr. Agrawal explained. “So until that tariff architecture comes back in place, the signing of a deal is something that I think will take some time. But concluding the negotiations and having everything ready will be something that we will strive to achieve as soon as possible.”
In particular, Mr. Agrawal spoke about the investigations undertaken by the American administration under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

One of these investigations, regarding forced labour, has been completed and a tariff of 10% has been levied on imports from India. The second investigation, looking into excess capacity, is yet to be completed and could come with further tariffs.

“There are certain 301 investigations which are already under review,” Mr. Agrawal said. “Those will also be coming to the fore in the next few weeks or months. You can’t have a deal until you have got uncertainty around multiple investigations which are already there.”

Separately, without mentioning the U.S. or any other country, Mr. Agrawal also asserted that trade deals can take a long time to conclude when parties try to maximise the benefits accruing to them rather than engaging in a spirit of compromise.

📰 India-U.S. trade deal signing will still ‘take some time’, says Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance

He added that the deal can be signed only after the U.S. finalises its new tariff framework. Recently, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the two nations had agreed that India would receive an advantage over its competitors

The actual signing of the India-U.S. trade will still “take some time”, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), adding that the negotiation part and the legal text will be completed soon.

The delay in signing, he said, was because it can be done only after the U.S. concludes its Section 301 investigations into its trade partners and finalises its tariff structure. A few days ago, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal asserted that the U.S. has acknowledged that India will receive lower tariffs as compared to its competitors.

“This is a deal that has been announced in February, the contours have already been announced as part of the joint statement,” Mr. Agrawal said while speaking at the curtain raiser of the FICCI Annual General Meeting. “The legal agreement has also been negotiated and it is now in final stages and it will be concluded soon.”

He was referring to the joint statement between India and the U.S. in February that announced the framework of an interim deal on trade.

However, Mr. Agrawal explained that the “challenge” is that this framework was announced against the background of the executive tariffs system that the U.S. President Donald Trump had put in place. At the time, the tariff on India was 50%. Later in February, the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the legal foundation of these tariffs.

“Now a new tariff architecture is being created by the U.S.,” Mr. Agrawal explained. “So until that tariff architecture comes back in place, the signing of a deal is something that I think will take some time. But concluding the negotiations and having everything ready will be something that we will strive to achieve as soon as possible.”

In particular, Mr. Agrawal spoke about the investigations undertaken by the American administration under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

One of these investigations, regarding forced labour, has been completed and a tariff of 10% has been levied on imports from India. The second investigation, looking into excess capacity, is yet to be completed and could come with further tariffs.

“There are certain 301 investigations which are already under review,” Mr. Agrawal said. “Those will also be coming to the fore in the next few weeks or months. You can’t have a deal until you have got uncertainty around multiple investigations which are already there.”

Separately, without mentioning the U.S. or any other country, Mr. Agrawal also asserted that trade deals can take a long time to conclude when parties try to maximise the benefits accruing to them rather than engaging in a spirit of compromise.

articles.title: UN Sustainable Development Goals group for science, technology rejigged
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development

The United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has reconstituted a 10-member group that works on promoting science, technology and innovation toward achieving its Sustainable Development Goals. The lone Indian in this group is former biologist and former Council of Scientific and Industrial Research CSIR Director General, Shekhar Mande, who is also currently President, Indian National Science Academy.
The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, while preparing for the 2027 SDG Summit.

“The group comprises distinguished experts from diverse geographic and disciplinary backgrounds from both developing and developed countries. Each member, recognised for their international excellence in science or technology, brings a wealth of experience and insight from civil society, the private sector, and the scientific community, underscoring the inclusive and comprehensive approach the UN is taking towards sustainable development,” an accompanying press statement noted.

The other members of the group are Marian Dorcas Quain (Ghana), Deputy Director-General of CSIR Ghana; Giorgio Rossi (Italy), Vice-President of Elettra-Sincrotrone Trieste; Magnus Andersson (Sweden), Associate Professor at Malmö University; Mônica Tejo Cavalcanti (Brazil), Professor at the Federal University of Campina Grande; Evgeniya Dmitrieva (Russia), Member of the Civic Chamber of the Russian Federation; Motoko Kotani (Japan), Executive Director of Science at RIKEN; Jin Li (China), President of Fudan University; Madin Maseeh (Maldives), President of the Maldives Space Research Organisation; and Rita Orji (Nigeria), Canada Research Chair in Persuasive Technology at Dalhousie University.
Professor Mande is also President of Vijnana Bharti, which, along with the Ministry of Science and Technology is gearing up to host the India International Science Festival in Pune in December.

Announcing this on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Union Minister of Science Jitendra Singh said at a press briefing that the government had taken a conscious decision to replace “scattered, repetitive gatherings”, including the erstwhile Indian Science Congress, with two flagship national events carrying distinct identities.

While the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in October saw 13 Ministries and Nobel Laureates, and was an academic-driven conclave exploring frontier themes, the India International Science Festival (IISF) brought a “festive, public-facing character with international resonance”. By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the western hub’s vibrant academic, research, and industrial ecosystem.

articles.title: Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well into 2027
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Saudi and Yemeni forces are ​now reorganising, with plans to protect Aden from the Houthi advances and potentially shift their offensive to eastern fronts where they have made some advances or have at least held their lines

Saudi Arabia is preparing for war against Yemen's Houthis to stretch well into next year, doubling down despite setbacks on the battlefield in Yemen ​and attacks disrupting life at home, said two Western officials briefed by Saudis on the plans.

The renewed conflict has become the most active front in ‌the wider Iran war, killing and wounding thousands and displacing hundreds of thousands in Yemen while derailing ​Saudi Arabia's efforts to draw in non-oil investment and host global events.
Public messaging around the war has also ⁠slowly shifted in the kingdom, with greater acknowledgement of its impacts.

Saudi officials now foresee the campaign stretching on for up to six months, aiming to see gains on the ground by the kingdom's Yemeni allies before any negotiations with the Houthis, according to Western officials, who spoke on condition ‌of anonymity to discuss non-public conversations with Saudi counterparts.
A third source familiar with the Saudi plans confirmed the accounts. All three said a deal to end the wider Iran war could see the Yemen conflict draw down.

The ‌third source also said Riyadh believes that U.S. offensive support for Saudi operations in Yemen, which President Donald Trump's administration has ‌so ⁠far withheld, could help change the tide of the conflict, potentially allowing Saudi-backed forces to make the gains ⁠they want within weeks.
A Saudi Foreign Ministry official declined to comment on the views of Saudi officials as described by the Western officials.

Saudi Arabia first entered the Yemen conflict in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to restore Yemen's government to power after the Houthis seized the ​capital Sanaa and much of the country. They fought to ‌a bloody stalemate and in 2022 reached a ceasefire that lasted until summer this year.

Since fighting restarted, the Houthis have seized the Red Sea coast and strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait from Saudi-backed forces, and encircled the city of Taiz in highlands above the government's temporary capital Aden on the southern coast.
Yemeni government forces mounted a counterattack last month, recapturing territory around the ‌strait, but withdrew over the past weekend to protect Aden in a major setback.

articles.title: Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears: Sources
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels; Eritrea, Sudan, Egypt ⁠all deny doing so

Ethiopia and Eritrea have amassed forces along their shared border, conflict monitors and people tied to militias in northern Ethiopia's Tigray ‌region said, fuelling fears of outright war between the historical rivals.

The build-up along the border has brought ​the two armies within striking distance of each other, according to the conflict monitors ACLED and the International ⁠Crisis Group, a person close to a pro-Ethiopian government militia in Tigray, and another person close to anti-government rebels there.

Reuters could not independently confirm reports of skirmishes between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces along the border. ACLED and a person close to the rebels said the ‌two sides had clashed in recent days, which would be their first direct armed exchanges in over a month, but the person close to the pro-Ethiopian government militia disputed this.

Reached for comment, Eritrean Information ‌Minister Yemane Gebremeskel decried "propaganda" from Ethiopia's ruling party about developments near the border but did not directly address reports about ‌military ⁠build-ups or clashes.
Spokespeople for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Diplomats and ⁠experts have warned of possible conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea since fighting broke out in September between Ethiopia’s federal government and rebels in Tigray, which borders Eritrea.

Witnesses and Ethiopia's government said Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October in support ​of the rebels. ACLED reported at the time ‌that drone strikes it believed were carried out by Ethiopia’s military had targeted the Eritrean troops. Ethiopia has not commented on the strikes.

Eritrea has denied any incursion into Ethiopia and accused Addis Ababa of seeking a pretext to invade its smaller neighbour, which was an Ethiopian province for three decades before gaining independence in 1993. They are now separated ‌by a border stretching more than 1,000 km (620 miles).

The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels. Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt ⁠all deny doing so.

Ethiopia and Eritrea have amassed forces along their shared border, conflict monitors and people tied to militias in northern Ethiopia's Tigray ‌region said, fuelling fears of outright war between the historical rivals.

The build-up along the border has brought ​the two armies within striking distance of each other, according to the conflict monitors ACLED and the International ⁠Crisis Group, a person close to a pro-Ethiopian government militia in Tigray, and another person close to anti-government rebels there.

Reuters could not independently confirm reports of skirmishes between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces along the border. ACLED and a person close to the rebels said the ‌two sides had clashed in recent days, which would be their first direct armed exchanges in over a month, but the person close to the pro-Ethiopian government militia disputed this.

Spokespeople for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Diplomats and ⁠experts have warned of possible conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea since fighting broke out in September between Ethiopia’s federal government and rebels in Tigray, which borders Eritrea.

Witnesses and Ethiopia's government said Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October in support ​of the rebels. ACLED reported at the time ‌that drone strikes it believed were carried out by Ethiopia’s military had targeted the Eritrean troops. Ethiopia has not commented on the strikes.

Eritrea has denied any incursion into Ethiopia and accused Addis Ababa of seeking a pretext to invade its smaller neighbour, which was an Ethiopian province for three decades before gaining independence in 1993. They are now separated ‌by a border stretching more than 1,000 km (620 miles).

The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels. Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt ⁠all deny doing so.

articles.title: Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel, Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year

The body overseeing U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to end the Gaza ‌war accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving ​the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ceasefire in danger of collapse.

The 12-page Board ⁠of Peace report, seen by Reuters , is the body's second to the United Nations Security Council since the U.S.-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a sobering assessment of progress made since then.
The Board, established and headed by Mr. Trump, is expected ‌to present the report's findings to a meeting of the council in New York at the end of November.

"The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains ‌the principal risk to the process," the report said, warning that "a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be ‌sustained ⁠indefinitely."

While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year.

Hamas agreed in July to a Board of Peace roadmap to surrender its weapons and transfer governance of Gaza to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected ​the roadmap, saying it will not withdraw until Hamas ‌is dismantled.
Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza, while the report said Hamas fighters have also continued attacks on Israeli troops.
"Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas' agreement to the roadmap to the test," the report said.
"Meanwhile, Hamas militant activity continues, the commitment to cease all military activities has not ‌been met in full by the parties, and the population faces another winter in tents and rubble."

Senior Hamas ​official Basem Naim dismissed the report as "pure disinformation", accusing the Board of Peace of providing cover to Israel to evade its commitments under the plan to end the war and to ⁠continue its aggression in Gaza.

articles.title: India, Canada eye defence pact during Modi visit in December
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa says both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests
India and Canada could be announcing a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s official visit in December, according to the country’s High Commissioner to Ottawa, Dinesh K. Patnaik.
Both countries are also in the final stages of negotiations of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. “We are on the cusp of finalising it,” Mr. Patnaik said.

Addressing a gathering in the Canadian capital organised by the Centre for Strategic Statecraft and the Canadian International Council, he said that both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests.

Mr. Patnaik took over as India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa in September 2025. Both countries had earlier expelled each other’s High Commissioners and reduced their diplomatic presence following the murder of Sikh Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in June 2023. Then Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau accused India of orchestrating the murder, throwing bilateral relations into a tailspin. Subsequent reports by Canadian agencies also listed India, alongside China and Russia, as an interferer in domestic politics. The turnaround in ties, which began with the mutual reinstatement of High Commissioners, is set to reach a milestone with Mr. Modi’s visit on December 11 and 12.

Mr. Patnaik said India and Canada are no longer talking about a reset of their derailed relations, but rather an overarching boost in ties spanning defence, space, nuclear energy, deep tech, trade, and the mobility of people. The two nations have moved from a complete lack of trust over a year ago to an unprecedented degree of mutual trust, he added.

“The fact is that in the core strategic concerns of Canada and India, there is no conflict. Still, all it took for the entire bilateral relationship to be derailed was the fringe diaspora issue,” he said, referring to the murder of Nijjar.

“The reason was the lack of trust. India believed that Canada was actively promoting separatism in India, and Canada believed India was organising violence in Canada. We had a series of meetings between senior Ministers, NSAs of both countries, and agencies at all levels as we set about rebuilding trust. Today, we have reached the highest levels of trust, where the most sensitive areas of cooperation, such as deep tech, defence, and space, are subjects of mutual cooperation,” Mr. Patnaik said.
Cooperation between Canadian and Indian agencies remains at a high level, the High Commissioner added.

articles.title: Researchers boost gut microbial activity linked to longevity in aged mice, find improved metabolism
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier ageing

Researchers have identified changes in the metabolic activity of the gut microbiome associated with exceptional longevity in humans, and found that amplifying the same activity in aged mice using engineered bacteria improved metabolic health.

Published in the journal Cell Metabolism , the team's study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier aging.

Senior author Amir Zarrinpar, chair in circadian biology and medicine, and professor of medicine at the University of California San Diego, said while many studies on aging focus on what goes wrong as one grows old, the findings suggest "some changes in the gut microbiome may actually represent the body's attempt to preserve metabolic health".
"If we can identify those beneficial functions and safely strengthen them, we may eventually be able to develop new ways to promote healthier aging," Zarrinpar said.

The gut microbiome, the community of bacteria and other microbes living in the digestive tract, is known to change throughout life and plays an important role in metabolism and inflammation, among other aspects of health.
Studies have also found distinctive microbiome features among people who age exceptionally well.
The researchers focused on how gut microbes modify bile acids, substances produced by the liver that help digest fats but also act as signalling molecules in the body.

Studying young and aged mice, they found that aging was associated with an increased microbial activity linked to enzymes called bile salt hydrolases. These enzymes chemically modify bile acids, allowing them to influence pathways involved in metabolism, inflammation and the body's internal clock.
The team also found greater bile acid modification in the mice.
To determine patterns in humans, they reanalysed publicly available data from a human ageing cohort, analysing bile acid measurements from 48 young adults, 107 older adults and 125 centenarians.

articles.title: Does India need to financially aid families’ decisions to have a child through fertility treatment?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Indian laws protect the decision not to have a child through statutes, schemes and subsidies, but the decision to have one is left to the mercy of the private assisted reproduction healthcare market

The reproductive-autonomy jurisprudence as evolved by the Supreme Court under Article 21 of the Constitution is rich yet narrow, focusing primarily on one side of the problem. In Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009), the Court held that reproductive choices may be exercised to procreate as well as to abstain from procreating. In X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department (2022), the Supreme Court extended the right to abortion to unmarried women as an exercise of ‘decisional autonomy’.

These, and nearly all other landmark cases are concerned only with an existing pregnancy. The freedom to pursue parenthood through medical treatment, however, has surfaced only at the margins. The Delhi High Court, in 2023, allowed parole of a life convict to attempt IVF, by recognising a “right to parenthood,” but only as a claim against a barrier the State itself had erected. No court has yet asked whether the State may leave a citizen’s access to infertility care entirely to their own purse. Can a right available to the fertile but structurally withheld from the infertile be called a universal right?

Science, Space & Environment Report: Does India need to financially aid families’ decisions to have a child through fertility treatment?. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a third cyclone in a month?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual, experts say

Andhra Pradesh is currently facing a rare weather phenomenon. Since October 28, the State has already been hit by two back-to-back cyclonic storms, and there is an imminent threat of another one battering the coastal districts in the next two days.

On October 28, the State was battered by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab , which made landfall near Narsapur in West Godavari district. On November 3, it was hit again by severe cyclonic storm Murasu , which made landfall close to Ongole in Prakasam district. Now, cyclonic storm Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall on November 20 between Narsapur and Puri.

Three tropical storms battering the coast within less than a month during the post-monsoon season is a rare scenario. The last times such a thing happened were in 1976, 1987 and 2013. Both 1976 and 1987 were El Niño years, and this year is also categorised as a super El Niño year .

When it comes to tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal, there are a number of driving factors, and El Niño is just one of them. Mostly, the formation of storms over the Bay, especially their frequency and intensity, differs slightly from the rest of the world, because the Bay of Bengal is almost a land-locked sea, said S.S.V.S. Ramakrishna, former head of the Department of Oceanography and Meteorology, Andhra University, who has spent over four decades researching the pattern of cyclones over the Bay.
“El Niño typically suppresses the southwest summer monsoon over India, but it has the opposite effect on the Northeast (winter) Monsoon and post-monsoon cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal,” he said.

During El Niño years, the northeast monsoon tends to be significantly more active over southern peninsular India. This creates continuous moisture convergence and frequent convective disturbances over the southern Bay, providing a steady assembly line of low-pressure areas.

And sometimes, in rare occurrences, remnants of a Pacific Ocean cyclone cross the Strait of Malacca, re-enter the Bay of Bengal, and intensify into a cyclone. “We had seen this phenomenon during the Odisha Super Cyclone in 1999,” he said.

Mr. Ramakrishna also pointed out that in October and November, the Bay of Bengal consistently retained high sea surface temperatures—over 26.5 degrees Celsius—and anything above 26 is conducive to developing a cyclonic system. This has been aided by the El Niño-modified upper-level wind patterns over the southern Bay of Bengal, which reduce vertical wind shear.

Another key factor that acted as a catalyst is the massive freshwater discharge from rivers like the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Godavari into the Bay of Bengal, which resulted in creating a low-salinity surface layer. This acts as a “barrier layer” that prevents cooler, deeper ocean water from mixing upward, so a passing cyclone (like Arnab or Murasu) does not cool the sea surface enough to stop the next storm from forming days later.

Persistent upper-tropospheric ridges (anticyclonic circulations) over the China–Myanmar region and central India have acted as steering barriers, blocking storms from recurving northeast and forcing them northwestward into the Andhra coast, he said.

articles.title: Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks

Demand for air purifiers in India has witnessed explosive growth in 2026, with major brands and retail platforms reporting sales doubling or tripling year-on-year. Driven by an early surge ahead of the traditional winter pollution season , consumer behaviour is shifting toward viewing indoor air quality as a year-round health priority rather than an emergency seasonal purchase.
According to industry leaders, adoption is gaining momentum well before peak pollution months.

Smart tech brand Qubo recorded a 150 percent growth over the previous year, while Xiaomi registered approximately 3X year-on-year sales growth during the festive period. Industry executives note that growing awareness surrounding indoor pollutants, ranging from dust and pet dander to everyday cooking and cleaning emissions, is encouraging households to take a proactive approach to home wellness throughout the year.

Retail footprint and online traffic reflect this expanding market footprint across the country. Electronics retailer Croma reported that air purifier sales volumes have more than doubled in 2026. While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks.
Premium tech maker Dyson also reported that visits to its air purifier pages grew by over 100 percent in October compared to the same period last year.

Modern buyers are increasingly seeking advanced functionality and intelligent filtration tech. Croma highlighted strong consumer interest in models featuring real-time AQI displays, app controls, and multi-functional units combining purification with humidification or heating.

On e-commerce platforms, Amazon India reported that sales doubled over the past week. Shoppers are actively leveraging Rufus, Amazon’s personalised AI shopping assistant, to filter models by room size, filter type, and live sensor capabilities, prompting the e-retailer to expand selection on Amazon Now for immediate delivery.

“We have observed a notable increase in consumer demand for air purifiers on Flipkart, reflected in higher search activity, product discovery and purchases. Northern India continues to account for a significant share of demand for the category. We also witnessed a rise in purchases during the early hours following Diwali, coinciding with heightened concerns around deteriorating air quality and the steps households are taking to manage their indoor environments,” said Flipkart.

articles.title: Clear the path: On SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India should use multilateral fora to advance bilateral cooperation

While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

articles.title: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

articles.title: Brace for impact: On rising inflation and external factors
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: High inflation due to external factors could soon exacerbate economic pain

India’s much-hyped domestic economic resilience is set to be tested over the next few months as external factors start to impose inescapable pressures. A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. While this is of some comfort, it is the higher wage earners that drive consumption in an economy. Real wage contraction for them, which is likely to have worsened in 2026, will hit consumption levels and private investment.

Further, there is strong evidence to suggest that the official inflation metrics are not capturing the full extent of rising prices. Data on cash with the public and UPI transactions show the value of both has been growing in double digits over the last year and more, significantly outpacing nominal GDP growth. This either suggests that the informal economy is far larger than earlier thought or, more likely, that inflation is well above what the official figures are being able to capture. Unfortunately, there are no real magic-wand fixes to this situation. Inflation is largely beyond the government’s control, and wage growth cannot happen overnight. The only way forward is to continue trying to spur sector-specific growth and warn people of the impending storm.

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 17 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: BJP holds key party meeting in Mathura for Assembly polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach

Senior BJP leaders from Uttar Pradesh, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, attended a key meeting at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Cow Research Institute in Parkham, Mathura, to discuss strategy for the upcoming U.P. Assembly polls.

The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach to counter the Opposition’s renewed pitch.

“One goal, one idea... BJP government again for the third time... Today, in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, I participated in a planning meeting with National General Secretary (Organisation) B.L. Santosh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and BJP Uttar Pradesh Incharge Shri Vinod Tawde,” wrote Pankaj Chaudhary, U.P. BJP president, on X.

“In the meeting, various important topics, including upcoming organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and providing benefits of public welfare schemes to every household, were discussed in detail. On this occasion, National General Secretary Irani, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya ji and Shri Brajesh Pathak, co-incharges of BJP Uttar Pradesh, Ministers of the State Government, public representatives, and state officials were present,” he added.

State Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya said the construction of a grand temple at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura will be a major poll issue in the 2027 U.P. elections, and that a grand Krishna temple will be built—through the courts or mutual dialogue, as with Ayodhya.
“If Akhilesh Yadav wants to join us in kar seva, we will take him along too to build a grand temple of Lord Krishna,” said the Deputy CM.

The meeting in Mathura is also significant amid the BJP’s emphasis on Mathura and western Uttar Pradesh. “The BJP holds meetings regularly to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment and other issues. Reach out to various sections of society is also part of our work,” said Dinesh Dubey, a senior BJP leader based in Lucknow.

Asad Rizvi, a political analyst based in Lucknow, said, “the meeting is significant as it is organised only a few months before the Assembly elections. Amid the main Opposition parties (the Samajwadi Party-Congress) pushing backwards, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Brahmins and marginalised groups through the PDA plank, the BJP will be recalibrating their policies and making a renewed effort towards them. ”

The SP president Akhilesh Yadav in a cryptic statement urged the BJP leaders to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. “I request them to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. It will be auspicious. If they fall ill, call a good doctor,” said Mr. Yadav.

articles.title: Tribute to Kartar Singh Sarabha, Punjab free from drugs and unemployment, says CM Mann
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said on Monday (November 16, 2026) that the greatest tribute to the 19-year-old revolutionary and freedom fighter Kartar Singh Sarabha is to fulfil his dream of a Punjab free from drugs, unemployment, and injustice.

He was speaking after paying tribute to Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha on his 111th martyrdom anniversary at his native village, Sarabha, in Ludhiana district. The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision.

“Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha embraced the gallows at the tender age of just 19, proving that courage, conviction and love for the motherland know no age. At a time when youngsters today are planning their futures, this great revolutionary was planning the liberation of the country. He sacrificed his youth, dreams and ultimately his life for our freedom,” he said.

“On November 16, 1915, Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha was hanged at Lahore Central Jail along with six other revolutionaries in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case. His fearless commitment to the freedom of the country remains a shining example of patriotism and selflessness,” he added.

As the Punjab 2027 Assembly election approaches, the drug menace has once again become a central campaign issue. In the run-up to the Assembly polls, the major political parties in the fray—the Congress, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)—are making the drug menace a key plank of their campaigns.

While the ruling party has been asserting that eradicating drugs is its “biggest priority,” the Opposition parties have accused the AAP of failing to curb the drug menace and instead patronising the drug trade.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said on Monday (November 16, 2026) that the greatest tribute to the 19-year-old revolutionary and freedom fighter Kartar Singh Sarabha is to fulfil his dream of a Punjab free from drugs, unemployment, and injustice.

He was speaking after paying tribute to Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha on his 111th martyrdom anniversary at his native village, Sarabha, in Ludhiana district. The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision.

“Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha embraced the gallows at the tender age of just 19, proving that courage, conviction and love for the motherland know no age. At a time when youngsters today are planning their futures, this great revolutionary was planning the liberation of the country. He sacrificed his youth, dreams and ultimately his life for our freedom,” he said.

“On November 16, 1915, Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha was hanged at Lahore Central Jail along with six other revolutionaries in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case. His fearless commitment to the freedom of the country remains a shining example of patriotism and selflessness,” he added.

As the Punjab 2027 Assembly election approaches, the drug menace has once again become a central campaign issue. In the run-up to the Assembly polls, the major political parties in the fray—the Congress, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)—are making the drug menace a key plank of their campaigns.

articles.title: Kishtwar killings aftermath: Remarks by Congress’ Karra, BJP’s Parihar spark protests in J&K
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Karra said that “two SPOs were killed by the Army in a mistaken-identity case on November 11”, while senior BJP leader Sharma said, “Congress is spreading misleading information to shift blame from terrorists to security forces”

Two separate remarks made by J&K Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra and BJP legislator Shagun Parihar in the aftermath of the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar on Monday (November 16, 2026) sparked protests from different quarters.

In response to the statement by Mr. Karra that “two SPOs were killed reportedly by the Army in a mistaken identity case on November 11”, senior BJP leader and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Sunil Sharma said, “The Congress is spreading misleading information to shift the blame from terrorists to our security forces. The SPOs were on duty and travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah to relieve the jawans posted there. Calling two martyrs hunters is an insult to their sacrifice and to their grieving families.”
He demanded that Mr. Karra “immediately withdraw the remarks and apologise to the martyrs’ families, the J&K Police and the Indian Army”.

Scores of members of the BJP and BJP-affiliated organisations held street protests against Mr. Karra and the Congress in Jammu. Members of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) also burn an effigy of Mr. Karra as a mark of protest.

BJYM leader Arun Prabhat, while condemning the statement of Mr. Karra, said, “It shows the hearts of Congress beat for Pakistan. The conspirators should face action. In case of any role of mosques, such places too should face action.”

Mr. Prabhat was seconding the controversial remarks of Ms. Parihar of the BJP, who claimed “announcements were made from the mosques in Kishtwar’s Dachhan area to identify the targets” allegedly ahead of the killings of two SPOs on November 11.

However, several religious organisations, including the Anjuman Islamia Bhaderwah and Kishtwar, in the Chenab Valley condemned the statement of Ms. Parihar and denied any role of mosques in the latest attack on the policemen. Ruling National Conference (NC) legislator Tanvir Sadiq said the BJP must be “held accountable for its MLA’s deeply irresponsible and inflammatory allegations against a mosque in Jammu”.

“Making communal allegations in the aftermath of a tragic killing is utterly unacceptable. The BJP leadership cannot hide behind silence or pretend this is an isolated matter. It must unequivocally condemn these remarks and issue an unconditional public apology. Stop playing with the communal harmony of J&K,” said Mr. Sadiq.

A spokesman of the All J&K Shia Association said the organisation “strongly condemn Ms. Parihar’s attempt to drag a mosque into the tragic killing of our brave SPOs”. “Terrorists are enemies of all humanity and terrorism has no religion. Unsubstantiated claims against a place of worship only weaken our fight against terror,” said the Association.
Jammu and Kashmir / Indian National Congress / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: Christian community seeks West Bengal CM’s intervention over targeted attacks ahead of Christmas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bishop of Calcutta Reverend Paritosh Canning ruled out claims of religious conversion by institutions affiliated with the Churches of North India

Ahead of the upcoming Christmas festivities, the representatives of Christian communities in West Bengal have expressed concerns about the rising attacks on churches across several districts in the State and have sought intervention from Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.

During a press conference addressed by the Bengal Christian Council (a cluster body for Protestant churches), the Bishop of Calcutta, Reverend Paritosh Canning, said that the concerns of the people of the community are not without reason.

“West Bengal has traditionally been a land of communal harmony, where people belonging to different faiths and communities have coexisted in peace, mutual respect, and brotherhood. With Christmas approaching, the apprehensions of the Christian community have become particularly serious. However, the prevailing atmosphere of insecurity has raised genuine concerns about whether Christians will be able to observe their religious services and celebrate festivals without fear or disruption,” the bishop said, speaking to media persons.

He added that such incidents have increased since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government came to power in West Bengal in May 2026. Attacks have been reported across several districts in South Bengal, on both banks of the Hooghly River, including South 24 Parganas, North 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, and Paschim Medinipur, among others.

Bishop Canning said that there are allegations of religious conversions in the churches, adding that “we can confirm that no conversion takes place at the churches operating under the Churches of North India.”
“All the minority communities used to live peacefully under the previous governments. However, it is not clear who the attackers are or why they are doing this,” he said.

In another development, representatives of Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP) held a meeting in response to remarks by West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya. The State BJP president had on Sunday said that religious conversions are taking place across districts in West Bengal and issued a warning to Christian missionary schools in the State, claiming that they are targeting teachers wearing saffron sarees.

The Archbishop of Calcutta (Roman Catholic), Reverend Elius Frank, also participated in a meeting organised by BCP, though he did not speak to the media. In a letter addressed to Samik Bhattacharya, Herod Mullick, the founder-secretary of BCP, said that “if any institution or individual is found guilty of illegal or forced religious conversion through greed or deception, we strongly condemn such actions and stand firmly against them.”

“However, making broad, unsubstantiated generalisations without naming specific individuals or institutions unfairly casts a shadow of suspicion over the entire Christian community and the more than 800 educational institutions we operate across West Bengal,” the letter added.

articles.title: Site inspection held for key Goshree-Mamangalam traffic corridor in Keralam’s Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Developing the stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads

People’s representatives and officials on Monday conducted a site inspection for the proposed Goshree-Mamangalam road development project, which is expected to provide major relief from traffic woes in Kochi.

The project is critical to improving the overall traffic system in the city and enhancing connectivity between various points. The demand for the proposed road dates back more than 30 years. Developing this stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads.

A sum of ₹1 crore was earmarked for the development of Goshree Bridge and Goshree-Mamangalam Road in the last State Budget following interventions by Hibi Eden MP, MLAs T.J. Vinod and Uma Thomas, and Mayor V.K. Minimol. The allocation was intended for conducting a traffic study, demarcating the alignment, and completing the survey. An action plan will be formulated based on scientific studies and survey findings.

Initially, the Goshree-Mamangalam road was proposed to be developed at 22 metres. However, during the tenure of the previous Kochi Corporation council, the width was scaled down to 15 metres in the 2024 Master Plan, which was subsequently approved by the State government. Based on this, follow-up measures are now being planned.

Coordination among various departments is essential, as several roads within the Kochi Corporation limits form part of the project. Accordingly, the PWD (Roads) will be entrusted with conducting the traffic study, carrying out the survey and preparing a detailed project report. This is expected to facilitate the efficient and time-bound execution of the project through coordinated efforts by the Corporation and the PWD.

The delegation assessed the existing condition of roads proposed to be included in the project, nature of traffic movement, development potential, and the role of the departments concerned. This is expected to aid the coordination of the proposed traffic study, survey, and subsequent follow-up measures.
MLAs T.J. Vinod and Uma Thomas, Mayor V.K. Minimol, and deputy mayor V.R. Sudheer were among those who participated in the inspection.

articles.title: A poverty line that falls short
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Reliable poverty estimates are not just for academic purposes. India has made real progress, but without a credible benchmark, it is hard to say how much, or how much remains to be done

There is no serious doubt that poverty in India has fallen sharply over the past decade. However, researchers and policymakers cannot agree on how many are still poor. Depending on the estimate, the share ranges from about 5% to more than 26%. Take the recent World Bank report. At its international line of $3 a day (2021 PPP), 2.6% of Indians were poor in 2022-23. Raise the line to $4.20, the bank’s benchmark for lower middle-income countries, and the figure jumps to around 16.1%. Same country, same year. Only the yardstick changed. A low level of extreme poverty does not necessarily mean poverty is not still a major issue. Where you draw the line decides how much economic insecurity you see.

India’s own figures tell a similar convoluted story. For example, SBI Research (2025) takes the Tendulkar line of 2009, adjusts it for inflation, and gets poverty of 7.2% in rural India and 4.6% in urban India for 2022-23. Rangarajan and Dev (2014), using an inflation-adjusted version of the Rangarajan Committee line, arrive at 10.8%. Further, Sethu, Surya and Ruthu (2024), who rebuild the Rangarajan method from the latest consumption survey, report 26.4%. Most of that gap boils down to the lines themselves: SBI’s Tendulkar-based lines use, after adjusting for inflation, about ₹1,632 a month per person in rural areas and ₹1,944 in urban areas. In contrast, Sethu et al. use much higher thresholds of ₹2,515 and ₹3,639. And the outcomes are obvious: Higher lines, higher poverty. Method matters too. One camp takes an old line and adjusts it for inflation. The other reconstructs the line from spending patterns in the new survey. Both have limitations, and they are answering different questions.
Macroeconomic & Financial Update: A poverty line that falls short. This development reflects key trends in India's fiscal roadmap, monetary policy transmission, and banking sector resilience.

fullParagraphs: Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com
Customers reported difficulty accessing the online accounts at some of the U.S.’ largest banks on Monday (November 16, 2026).
Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com.
Chase Bank’s services are experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said Monday (November 16, 2026).

“Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.”
The reports follow a major outage by Microsoft that began on Friday (November 13, 2026) and lasted for hours, which impacted services including Outlook, Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
Some Chase customers received a message that said, “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

articles.title: ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: PM Modi to participate in ASEAN-India Summit; Quad meeting likely after President Trump arrives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In the first Quad Summit since 2024, PM Modi is expected to meet U.S. President Trump, Japanese PM Takaichi and Australian PM Albanese
“India, ASEAN represent around one-fourth of global population; it is important to decide our future by cooperation; not by competition,” PM Modi said in the India-ASEAN Summit in Manila today.
“We believe that India’s development and ASEAN’s prosperity are deeply interconnected,” he added.

The Embassy of India in Manila will resume all regular consular services, passport applications and visa processing from Wednesday, following a temporary suspension in view of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and East Asia Summit.

According to the earlier advisory, the closure was in accordance with Proclamation No. 1447 issued by the Government of the Republic of the Philippines, declaring special non-working days in the National Capital Region (NCR) for the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.

Joint Statement of the 29th ASEAN-Japan Summit on Realising Economic Resilience was adopted today in Manila, with the meeting being attended by the Leaders of ASEAN Member States, the Prime Minister of Japan H.E. Sanae Takaichi, and Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn.

In the ASEAN leaders’ meeting today, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi pledged to work with ASEAN to boost regional economic and energy resilience to address export restrictions and vulnerabilities from rapid AI development, and strengthen supply chains, including on critical minerals.

A Japanese Foreign Ministry official said it was expected that Quad leaders would try to show unity, with maritime security, export restrictions, critical-minerals supply-chain diversification and AI among potential discussion points.
U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive in China on Wednesday, for an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, following his meeting with the Quad leaders today.

This Quad alliance is heavily criticised by China, given that one of its purposes is to support Indo-Pacific nations in strengthening their sovereignty and simultaneously constrain China’s attempts to undermine that capacity-building.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to attend the Quad leaders’ meeting, the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit during his ongoing visit to the Philippines, External Affairs Ministry (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Tuesday.
